the pilus of Geobacter species is a highly conductive protein nanowire that can transfer electrons to Fe(III) oxide minerals, electrodes and other extracellular electron acceptor.

molecular dynamics simulations of Geobacter conductive pili revealed that the aromatic amino acids cluster along the pilus and form a helical band that is interspersed in regions of highest negative potentials.

the pilin protein is organized as a right-handed aromatic helix that is interspersed with negatively charged residues and small positive foci, and these configurations are important for the function of the pilus as an electrical nanowire.
